entry.description: stop `LoggingEvent.UserName` reporting the wrong user for an event logged while impersonating. The property resolved the identity of whichever thread read it, so with a buffering appender the buffered events were attributed to the thread flushing the buffer rather than the one that logged them (CWE-282). An event logged while impersonating now takes its user name with it when it is fixed, and an event read on an impersonating thread reports the not available text instead of that thread's user. Without impersonation the name is the process identity, which is the same on every thread, so it is still resolved lazily and nothing changes (audit 1231d72-f014)
